questions.prompt: What is the pressure regulator's main role?
questions.explanation: The regulator adjusts the pressure supplied to control and power circuits.
questions.section: Pressure Regulator in a Circuit, slide 21

reviewCue.text: Review C209 Pneumatic Systems.pdf, slide 21. Look for Pressure Regulator in a Circuit, slide 21.
reviewCue.excerpt:
Pressure Regulator in a Circuit
► As shown, the regulator with the pressure 
gauge us used to reduce the supply pressure 
to the control and power circuit of the 
machine.
► Normally it is located in the circuit between a 
filter and the control valves.
► A pressure regulator contains:
► Adjustment knob
► Spring (loading element)
► Diaphragm or piston (sensing element)
► Poppet/seat (control valve)
► Optional relief valve
► A needle valve is not one of these 
components. It is a separate flow-control 
device, not a pressure-reducing 
mechanism.

questions.prompt: What does an air filter remove from supply air?
questions.explanation: Ambient air contains contaminants; the filter cleans particles and water droplets from it.

reviewCue.text: Review C209 Pneumatic Systems.pdf, slide 22. Look for Air Filter, slide 22.
reviewCue.excerpt:
Air Filter
Function
► The air used in pneumatics is ambient air. That 
means that the air can contain dust, 
pollution, and other particles which are to 
small to see.
► If a particle is large enough it can prevent 
close fitting parts from working smoothly.
► An air filter is a device designed to clean the 
air before it enters the pneumatic system. It 
will also remove water droplets from the air 
supply. 
► All pneumatic system should be installed with 
one or more air filters to keep them working 
properly.

questions.prompt: What connects the air supply to the rest of the pneumatic circuit?
questions.explanation: Supply line. The course explains: Basic Components Conductors Conductors (hose/pipe) are needed to transmit air between pneumatic system components. The Supply Line connects the compressed air source to the control devices. The Actuator line carries the air to and from the control devices to the actuator. Returned air is exhausted back into the atmosphere through an exhaust port.

questions.prompt: What does a pneumatic pressure gauge indicate?
questions.explanation: System pressure. The course explains: Pressure Gauges Functionality Indicates the amount of pressure in a pneumatic system. Technicians read these gauges to determine if the machine is operating properly. Most gauges have a face plate graduated in either US customary (Psi), or Si units (Pascals). A pointer rotates around the scaled face plate as the pressure changes to indicate the pressure in the system. Pressure Gauge error Manufacturers state the error of the gauge in their catalogs as a percent of the full scale reading. A small percentage of gauge error is always possible.

questions.prompt: Which regulator component restricts airflow to control downstream pressure?
questions.explanation: Poppet. The course explains: Pressure Regulators The poppet controls downstream pressure by restricting the airflow. The piston is attached to one end of the poppet to provide a surface for the spring to push on. The adjustment spring allows for smooth adjustment of the regulator. The adjustment knob changes the compression on the spring which controls the level of downstream pressure.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the filter deflector plate?
questions.explanation: Spin the incoming air. The course explains: Air Filter Inlet Port – Air enters filter through inlet port. Deflector Plate – The deflector plate causes the air to spin inside the filter bowl. Filter element – The filter element traps the remaining small particles. Baffle – The baffle controls the path of the air flow. Bowl – The bowl collects the water and dirt particles and serves as the outer casing of the air filter. Manual drain – The drain plug allows the collected water and dirt particles to be drained. Water should be drained before it reaches the bottom of the baffle. Outlet Port – The air exits the filter through the outlet port. Inlet Port Outlet Port Deflector Plate Filter Element Baffle Bowl Manual Drain A01 A38

questions.prompt: What does a tee fitting connect to a supply line?
questions.explanation: Two branch circuits. The course explains: Tee and Cross Fittings Symbol Connects two different circuits to the same supply line. Uses a single fitting called a tee. A tee symbol is use to show the branching connections in a pneumatic circuit. Gauge Block Tees Gauge block tees do the same thing as loose fitting tees. Machined from blocks of aluminum. Tees are often directly connected to pressure gauges because they allow easy connection of a pressure gauge to monitor the pressure in a line.

questions.prompt: What do piston seals separate in a double-acting cylinder?
questions.explanation: The two cylinder chambers. The course explains: Double-Acting Pneumatic Cylinder Piston seals – piston seals are used to separate the chambers of the cylinder. These seals allow pressure to build and reduce leakage inside the cylinder. Rod seals – A flexible seal, called a rod seal, is placed around the piston rod to prevent external leakage. Rod bushing – a bushing holds the piston in place and helps support the rod as it extends. Piston Seal Rod seal Bushing

questions.prompt: Which DCV port is connected to the air supply?
questions.explanation: P. The course explains: 5-Port, 3-Postion DCV Valve body – the valve body has ports to provide flow paths for the fluid. Each of the ports is labeled according to its connection. Operator – The operator is the device that moves the spool. An operator can be a lever, electrical solenoid, a manual push button, or other control device. Spool – The spool is designed with lands that channel the flow through he valve to specific ports. Shifting positions changes flow paths. Springs – a 3-postion valve usually has a spring on either side of the spool to position it in the middle when not energized. questions.prompt: What happens in the blocked center position of the 5/3 valve shown in the course?
questions.answer: All ports are blocked and the cylinder holds position
options: All ports are blocked and the cylinder holds position
Both cylinder ports receive unrestricted supply
All ports are connected to exhaust
questions.explanation: All ports are blocked and the cylinder holds position. The course explains: 5-Port, 3-Postion DCV A 5/3 DCV is usually connected to air cylinder so that port A extends the rod and port B s it. P connects to the air supply, and EA and EB exhaust to the atmosphere. When the spool is in the middle position, air flow is blocked between all ports. This causes the cylinder to hold its position.
